governing_intent: Implement the FD-05-constrained durable operational store for Python execution coordination: crash-safe canonical operational state, effectively once-only effects, fenced reservations, and recoverable restart state without expanding into factory-loop, vendor, evidence-store, or Node work.
summary: PY-03 is bounded by approved authority, cleanly follows PY-02, honestly claims partial requirement coverage, and specifies observable SQLite-backed executable proof. No Founder or architecture decision must be invented.
implementation_unknowns: Concrete typed OperationalStore port shapes consistent with accepted PY-02 values and outcomes.
SQLite schema, transaction boundaries, indexes, and migration representation.
Deterministic subprocess crash harness and idempotent-effect/read-back fixture design.
Adapter-composition mechanism for the future PostgreSQL conformance run.
verification_assessment: Verification is real executable proof: a real SQLite file, actual process termination at every named durable boundary, restart recovery checks, duplicate and stale-write rejection, fencing, schema fail-closed behavior, port-only conformance, retained outputs with real exit statuses, existing Python fitness checks, and the Node suite. Simulated exceptions alone are expressly insufficient.
material_risks: Implementation must begin only from the released baseline containing accepted PY-02; its absence is a sequencing constraint, not a contract ambiguity.
The currently inspected main checkout has unrelated untracked files, so a clean baseline must be established before implementation begins.
Crash proof must exercise a genuine durable effect/read-back seam so once-only behavior is not only an in-memory artifact.
next_action: Record PY-03 as READY; after PY-02 acceptance, establish the required clean released baseline and authorize implementation under this contract.
rationale: Approved authority fixes the ownership boundary, durability model, profile isolation, effect semantics, storage direction, migration safety, and coexistence constraints. The remaining choices are normal implementation design. Inbox, effect intent/outbox, reservations, recovery, schema safety, and conformance form one transactional operational-store concern; splitting them would weaken the required atomic guarantees.

provider_evidence.note: reassessment after SWF-16..20 closure-policy contract normalization and PY-02 DONE
